output.brief:
The wrong expiry dates did not come from the agency operators or the printer upgrade. Printer job records show that from 4 Oct the data sent to the printer already carried a 36-month shelf life, and no operator overrode anything. Before that, all 30 Veltranol jobs were correct, including those run by agency operators after the firmware change. The ERP shows Regulatory Affairs entered 36 months on 3 Oct, but it was meant to apply only from 1 Mar 2027. The line integration service used it early, which contradicts what the vendor says it does. Two faulty lots also ran on Line 1 day shift with permanent staff, so this is not a night-shift or agency problem. The camera only checks print against the job, so it passed every carton.

Next steps:
- Don't warn or remove the agency operators.
- Reset the Veltranol shelf-life record so only the currently approved value can be read.
- Hold every Veltranol lot packed since 4 Oct, including the two in the warehouse.
- Add a second-person check of printed expiry against the batch record at each setup.
- Check the other products edited in October, especially the two with future-dated values.
- Ask the vendor and IT why the future-dated value was used.
- Keep the camera check switched on.

I'm fairly confident in the cause. I haven't confirmed why the integration service ignored the valid-from date, or whether other products are affected.
